currentContext.business: Graphite India's core Graphite and Carbon segment (about 89% of revenue) manufactures graphite electrodes and other carbon/graphite products for electric arc furnace steelmaking, backward-integrated into Calcined Petroleum Coke (CPC) and carbon/tamping paste, plus Impervious Graphite Equipment (IGE) for corrosive-process industries such as chemicals, fertilizers and pharma intermediates. Its Steel segment (Powmex Steels Division) is India's largest manufacturer of High-Speed Steel used in cutting tools for automotive, machine tools, aviation and retail markets. Other operations include captive wind, solar and hydel power generation, a GRP pipes business being wound down, and a newly announced diversification into Synthetic Graphite Anode Material (SGAM) for lithium-ion battery cells.

risks.note: The Company's business is closely linked to the global steel industry, particularly the cyclical EAF-based steelmaking segment; any slowdown in steel-consuming sectors such as construction, infrastructure, automotive and manufacturing could reduce steel production levels and consequently graphite electrode demand.

risks.risk: Raw material price and availability risk
risks.note: Graphite electrode pricing and margins depend on availability and pricing of key raw materials - petroleum needle coke, raw petroleum coke and coal tar pitch - as well as coking coal prices; supply disruptions or fluctuations in global crude oil / petroleum-linked markets could raise production costs.

The United States has initiated antidumping and countervailing duty investigations against imports of Large Diameter Graphite Electrodes from India and China, and Brazil has initiated similar investigations; the outcome could affect the terms of US market access for Indian producers such as the Company.

risks.risk: Rising global trade barriers and carbon-related regulation
risks.note: Global steel and graphite electrode markets remain vulnerable to trade-related restrictions, safeguard duties, anti-dumping measures and rapidly evolving carbon-related regulations across regions, adding uncertainty to export opportunities and market conditions.

risks.risk: China steel overcapacity and export pressure
risks.note: Elevated Chinese steel exports (estimated around 118 MT in 2025) continue to influence global steel prices and competitive intensity, indirectly pressuring realisations across the steel and graphite electrode value chain.

risks.risk: Power-intensive cost structure / energy cost exposure
risks.note: Graphite electrode manufacturing is power intensive; any increase in power tariffs or energy costs, together with freight cost volatility, may affect overall cost structures and profitability.

The Company is exposed to currency volatility given its balanced exposure to exports and imports across multiple geographies; while a natural hedge exists from diversified currency exposure, volatility may still affect realisations, procurement costs and profitability.

The graphite electrode industry remains highly competitive, with competition based on pricing, product quality, operational performance, delivery reliability and customer relationships, making sustained competitiveness important for maintaining market position and profitability.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Graphite India is one of the leading global producers of graphite electrodes by capacity, with over six decades of technical expertise, serving electric-arc-furnace steelmakers worldwide alongside diversified carbon, impervious graphite equipment and high-speed steel businesses.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Graphite India's core Graphite and Carbon segment (about 89% of revenue) manufactures graphite electrodes and other carbon/graphite products for electric arc furnace steelmaking, backward-integrated into Calcined Petroleum Coke (CPC) and carbon/tamping paste, plus Impervious Graphite Equipment (IGE) for corrosive-process industries such as chemicals, fertilizers and pharma intermediates. Its Steel segment (Powmex Steels Division) is India's largest manufacturer of High-Speed Steel used in cutting tools for automotive, machine tools, aviation and retail markets. Other operations include captive wind, solar and hydel power generation, a GRP pipes business being wound down, and a newly announced diversification into Synthetic Graphite Anode Material (SGAM) for lithium-ion battery cells.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Graphite and Carbon:** Graphite Electrodes (including large-diameter and UHP), Miscellaneous Carbon and Graphite Products, Calcined Petroleum Coke (CPC) - aluminium and graphite grades, Carbon Paste, Electrically Calcined Anthracite Paste, Electrode Paste, Tamping Paste, Impervious Graphite Equipment (IGE) and Spares
- **Steel:** High Speed Steel (HSS), Alloy Steel
- **Other Segments:** Glass Reinforced Plastic (GRP) Pipes (operations being closed)
- **New Initiative:** Synthetic Graphite Anode Material (SGAM) - planned diversification

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Electric arc furnace (EAF) based steelmaking, globally
- Chloro-Alkali, crop protection agrochemicals, chlorinated organics, specialty & fine chemicals, phosphoric acid, fertilizers, rayon, steel pickling, metal processing, polymers, drug intermediates, batteries and gelatine (IGE end-uses)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global crude steel demand is forecast to grow only 0.3% in 2026 before improving 2.2% in 2027, supported by a gradually improving demand environment in developed economies (EU, US, Japan, Korea) and continued growth in developing markets, particularly India
- Global (excluding China) EAF-based steel production is growing faster than BOF-based production, with EAF capacity expected to grow at approximately 3-4% CAGR through 2030 - a structural driver of UHP graphite electrode demand
- Domestic Indian steel demand is expected to grow 9-10% in FY 2026-27, driven by government infrastructure capital expenditure on roads, railways, housing and industrial projects; India's installed steel capacity (~220 MT in FY26) is expected to expand toward a 300 MT target by FY 2030-31
- China's elevated steel exports (~118 MT in 2025) and continued real-estate-led demand weakness are keeping global steel prices and competitive intensity under pressure, though China's demand contraction is expected to slow in 2026 and stabilise in 2027
- Rising adoption of green steel / low-carbon production is a medium-term theme: India's green steel demand is expected to reach around 4.49 MT by FY 2029-30, and the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), in its definitive phase from January 2026, is making decarbonisation a competitive necessity for steel exporters
- Graphite and Carbon segment performance improved on higher production/sales volumes and lower costs, partly offset by lower realisations, reflecting a demand-recovery-but-pricing-pressure dynamic in the graphite electrode market
- Key raw material cost/availability risk (petroleum needle coke, raw petroleum coke, coal tar pitch, coking coal, energy/freight costs) continues to be flagged as a margin driver given the power-intensive nature of graphite electrode manufacturing

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Diversification into manufacturing Synthetic Graphite Anode Material (SGAM), used in lithium-ion battery cells for the EV ecosystem, to generate a new revenue stream
- Continued focus on large-diameter and ultra-high power (UHP) graphite electrodes, the grades preferred by major steel manufacturers, leveraging over six decades of technical expertise in the industry
- Positioning to cater to demand from both domestic and international steel manufacturers as Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) based steelmaking gains share of global steel production

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: This routed excerpt does not carry the Company's headline graphite-electrode capacity expansion narrative; instead it discloses site-level environmental/social and safety-related capital and R&D spend under BRSR Principle 2. In FY 2025-26 the Company reported 67% of R&D investment (against 0.27% in FY 2024-25) and 4% of capex (against 52.9% in FY 2024-25) directed at technologies improving environmental and social impacts. Named site-level improvements included: at the Durgapur plant, a fume hood with scrubber unit for chemical testing/acid treatment, a vibratory cup mill to eliminate manual sampling and reduce dust emissions, and a pilot extrusion press (up to 50 mm dia) for improved process capability; at the Baruni (Barauni) plant, water coolers, a bag stacker machine to reduce manual handling, lightning arrestors, and motorcycle parking stands; at the Angul plant, water coolers, solar panel installation to promote renewable energy use, a horizontal lifeline for work-at-height safety, and strengthened emergency evacuation systems; and at the Titilagarh plant, water coolers, PNG conversion for improved energy efficiency and lower emissions, and a fire-fighting system installation.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Over six decades of technical expertise in graphite electrode manufacturing, one of the leading global producers by capacity, with focus on large-diameter and ultra-high power (UHP) electrodes preferred by major steel manufacturers
- Backward integration into Calcined Petroleum Coke (CPC) production at Barauni for electrode raw material security
- Powmex Steels Division is the single largest manufacturer of High-Speed Steel in India with almost 100% penetration across major domestic OEMs
- ~80% of energy consumption at the Nashik graphite electrode plant met through renewable energy (captive wind and solar), reducing power costs and carbon emissions
- Recognised export performance: Four-Star Export House status and multiple EEPC national/regional export excellence awards

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Cyclicality of EAF-based steelmaking demand — The Company's business is closely linked to the global steel industry, particularly the cyclical EAF-based steelmaking segment; any slowdown in steel-consuming sectors such as construction, infrastructure, automotive and manufacturing could reduce steel production levels and consequently graphite electrode demand.
- Raw material price and availability risk — Graphite electrode pricing and margins depend on availability and pricing of key raw materials - petroleum needle coke, raw petroleum coke and coal tar pitch - as well as coking coal prices; supply disruptions or fluctuations in global crude oil / petroleum-linked markets could raise production costs.
- Trade-defence investigations in export markets — The United States has initiated antidumping and countervailing duty investigations against imports of Large Diameter Graphite Electrodes from India and China, and Brazil has initiated similar investigations; the outcome could affect the terms of US market access for Indian producers such as the Company.
- Rising global trade barriers and carbon-related regulation — Global steel and graphite electrode markets remain vulnerable to trade-related restrictions, safeguard duties, anti-dumping measures and rapidly evolving carbon-related regulations across regions, adding uncertainty to export opportunities and market conditions.
- China steel overcapacity and export pressure — Elevated Chinese steel exports (estimated around 118 MT in 2025) continue to influence global steel prices and competitive intensity, indirectly pressuring realisations across the steel and graphite electrode value chain.
- Power-intensive cost structure / energy cost exposure — Graphite electrode manufacturing is power intensive; any increase in power tariffs or energy costs, together with freight cost volatility, may affect overall cost structures and profitability.
- Foreign currency fluctuation — The Company is exposed to currency volatility given its balanced exposure to exports and imports across multiple geographies; while a natural hedge exists from diversified currency exposure, volatility may still affect realisations, procurement costs and profitability.
- Industry competitive intensity — The graphite electrode industry remains highly competitive, with competition based on pricing, product quality, operational performance, delivery reliability and customer relationships, making sustained competitiveness important for maintaining market position and profitability.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Diversification into manufacturing Synthetic Graphite Anode Material (SGAM), used in lithium-ion battery cells for the EV ecosystem, to generate a new revenue stream
- Continued focus on large-diameter and ultra-high power (UHP) graphite electrodes, the grades preferred by major steel manufacturers, leveraging over six decades of technical expertise in the industry
- Positioning to cater to demand from both domestic and international steel manufacturers as Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) based steelmaking gains share of global steel production
